div.p: iravukkuṟi vantu nīṅkun talaimakaṉai yetirppaṭṭut tōḻi colliyatu.
What the confidante said when encountering HIM who was leaving after having come to the night tryst.

lg.l: ūruñ cēriyu muṭaṉiyain talareḻat
[tēro]ṭu maṟu[ki]yum paṇimoḻi payiṟṟiyuṅ
keṭāat tīyi ṉurukeḻuc cellūrk
kaṭāa yāṉaik kuḻūuccaman tataiya
maṉmaruṅ kaṟutta maḻuvā ṇeṭiyōṉ
muṉmuyaṉ ṟaritaṉiṉ muṭitta vēḷvik
kayiṟarai yātta kāṇṭaku vaṉappi
ṉaruṅkaṭi neṭuntūṇ pōla yāvaruṅ
kāṇa lākā māṇe[ḻi] lāka
muḷḷutoṟum paṉikku neñciṉai nīyē
neṭumpuṟa nilaiyiṉai varuntiṉai yāyiṉ
muḻaṅkukaṭa lōtaṅ kālaik koṭkum
paḻampaṉ ṉelli ṉūṉū rāṅka
ṇōlā virumpuṭ pōla neñcamarntu
kātaṉ māṟāk kāmar puṇarcciyi
ṉiruṅkaḻi mukanta ceṅkō lavvalai
[mu]ṭaṅkupu[ṟa] viṟavō ṭiṉamīṉ ceṟikku
neṭuṅkatirk kaḻaṉit taṇcāayk kāṉat
tiyāṇart taṇpaṇai yuṟumeṉa kāṉa
lāya māynta cāyiṟaip paṇaittō
ṇalleḻil citaiyā vēmañ
colliṉit teyyayān teḷiyu māṟē.
Having whirled along with [your] chariot and repeated humble words
so that gossip arose equally in the village and in the quarter,
o you with a heart that trembles each time you remember
[her] glorious [and] graceful bosom, not to be seen
by anyone, like the heavily protected tall pillar,
of a beauty fit to be seen, to the bottom of which a rope is tied
for the sacrifice that was completed with difficulty(?), making an effort in front
of the tall one with an axe for a weapon, who cut open the side of kings,
when the battle was packed with a crowd of rutting elephants,
in awe-inspiring Cellūr with [its] unextinguished fire(?),
- in case you should suffer from standing outside for a long [time],
speak now, in a way that we understand,
of protection, so that the good grace is not wasted
in [her] bamboo shoulders with flexible joints, chosen among the companions
in the seashore grove, [with the words]: “it resembles the fertile cool bamboo
of cool Cāaykkāṉam, [surrounded by] fields with long ears,
where the pretty nets with straight rods that are drawn from the dark backwaters
tighten over various fish together with hunch-backed prawn”,
[not wasted] in [this] passionate union, love unchanging,
hearts remaining like big birds that cannot endure(?),
there in Ūṉūr of old with much rice,
where time revolves with the flood of the thundering sea.
